thread:
Priya: Quick heads-up — onboarding Orbitron LoRA + multi-embed support. I pushed a quick eval pack to s3://redwood-evals/orbitron/multiembed/ and linked it in the console. Initial smoke shows embedding L2 norms shifted for intents A/B, looks systemic, not just noise.

Tom: link?

Priya: https://console.redwood/evals/orbitron/multiembed (private) :shrug:

Aisha: Results? numbers?

Priya: paraphrase accuracy down ~2.4% on the customer suite, retrieval MRR -0.03. Small but consistent across seeds and prompt templates.

Kai: Did you merge the tokenizer/tokenmap? We saw token ID offsets with multi-embed tokenizers before — can cause silent embedding shifts.

Priya: Not applied yet. The LoRA weights were merged with `merge_lora.py --compat-mode smart` but the merge step emitted token remap warnings:

```
WARN: tokenizer offset mismatch: base_vocab_size=50257 adapter_vocab_size=50260
INFO: generating token remap table -> /tmp/tokenmap_5123.json
Apply token remap? yes
```

Tom: Try the tokenmap aligner: `scripts/tokenmap/align_vocab.py --from-base --apply --report` — it makes the remap deterministic and writes a report.

Priya: Ran aligner. It removed 7 OOV entries and produced a map, but embedding norms still shifted (see artifacts).

Aisha: Could this be quantization interaction? What precisions did you try?

Priya: Baseline fp16, int8 (per-channel) and int4 simulated. Quick numbers:

```
MODEL=orbitron-lora-multiembed
EVAL=quick_embed_smoke
TIME=2026-03-21T12:10Z
FP16: MRR=0.782
INT8: MRR=0.779
INT4: MRR=0.763
```

Priya: Note: int8 is within noise, int4 shows larger drop. Also saw different behavior when prefix/KV caching was enabled.

Kai: That hints at KV cache / runtime ordering issues — multi-embed concatenation can shift KV offsets if layernorm/merge ordering differs between patched adapter and runtime kernel assumptions.

Tom: Repro steps: run eval with `--no-cache` and `--disable-prefix` and compare with/without tokenmap. Also capture runtime trace.

Priya: Queued the no-cache runs and a runtime trace. Snippet from the smoke trace:

```
TRACE: model_init layer_order=pre_norm
TRACE: adapter_injected position=after_attn
WARN: kv_offset_mismatch detected at step=18
```

DevEvalBot: Smoke pack run complete — artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/orbitron/smoke/5123456789 ; summary.json -> s3://.../summary.json

Aisha: If int4 remains unstable, recommend we mark int4 as "experimental" for Orbitron and default to int8 for Dedicated customers. We should include guidance in the catalog entry and the canary plan.

Priya: Agreed. I'll draft a model-catalog PR with: merge notes, tokenmap applied, quantization recommendations (fp16/int8 recommended, int4 experimental), and a canary rollout: 10% traffic -> monitor MRR + hallucination alerts + token-level latency breakdown.

Kai: Also flag runtime team to check KV offset handling for adapter-inserted concatenation patterns — adding a small unit test would help catch regressions.

Priya: Created GH issue #1798 for runtime KV test and a PR branch `orbitron/lora-onboard` for the catalog.

Tom: Ping @security for a quick review of fine-tune prompts — customer mentioned some PII in a training doc.

Priya: Pinged @security.

Aisha: Nice. If we stabilize int4 later we can add a quant-profile in Redwood Optimize to auto-suggest it per workload.

Priya: Thanks all :thumbsup: Will follow up with the PR and a short postmortem if we need a rollback during canary.
